story:
With a sharp *clang*, the vase shattered into pieces on the floor, and Garfiel could only stand there in stunned silence, eyes wide in disbelief.

“Sh-shit, I went and did it…”

His outstretched hand, with nowhere to go, hovered aimlessly in the air, and Garfiel couldn’t help but clench his teeth to stop them from chattering.

It had been a sudden tragedy, the moment he’d stretched up in the hallway. The instant his fingertips brushed something hard, the vase on the decorative shelf had flipped upside down—a piercing death knell echoing through the air.

It was a blue vase. He had no idea if it was expensive or cheap, but looking at the pattern on the shards, it somehow felt like it must’ve cost a fortune. And anyway, this was the Roswaal manor—there was no way they’d have anything tacky like a bargain-bin knockoff.

“Ngh, sometimes the cap’n messes around with Beatrice on pottery challenges, so there’s a chance this was one of those… but that’d be even worse!”

Even if it was a bit misshapen, Garfiel pictured Beatrice proudly showing off her finished pieces, and he carefully inspected the broken vase. At least it didn’t seem like amateur work, which brought him a small sigh of relief.

“—So that’s what the noise was. You really screwed up, huh, Garf.”

“Wha—!? R-Ram!?”

“Yes, Ram. But it’s not just Ram.”

Startled by the voice from behind, he jumped so high he nearly cracked his head on the ceiling. Turning around with trepidation, Garfiel’s vision filled with Ram—arms crossed over her chest—and beside her, her familiar sister, brows faintly furrowed.

“Oh, Sis was here too, huh? I-It wasn’t on purpose!”

“— . There’s no reason we’d suspect that. It’s you, after all, Garf. You probably just swung your arms around without looking where you were going, right?”

“Y-Yeah, you get it. As expected of Sis.”

“What’s with the ‘as expected’? Don’t think flattery’s gonna get you anywhere.”

Reprimanded by Frederica’s prim, upturned expression, Garfiel hunched his shoulders.

For some reason, Garfiel could never quite stand tall in front of Frederica. Sure, she was his sister, but he always felt like she caught him at his worst.

He was always thinking he wanted to prove her wrong, show her he could do better.

“Sis, ain’t there some punk around I could just blast away right now?”

“What are you even talking about, all of a sudden? More importantly, there are shards everywhere—step back. This is… going to need tools to clean up. Ram.”

“The cleaning supplies are at the end of the hall.”

“I know that without you telling me! Go fetch them!”

“Fine. Come on, Garf.”

Jerked along by her chin, Garfiel had no time to resist before he was following. Catching up to the slender back ahead of him, he ground his fangs with a faint click.

“Screwed up big time…”

“Frederica knows it wasn’t on purpose. Don’t beat yourself up too much.”

“Yeah, I know, but… I figured I’d get chewed out, so not getting it makes it hit harder, y’know? You get me, right?”

“—?”

“That’s the face of someone who doesn’t get it!”

“I’m so used to not getting scolded that it didn’t even click. …But yes. If there’s one thing Ram can say…”

“One thing… what?”

“The vases and flowers on display in the manor? Frederica picked out that interior herself.”

“————”

“For you, Garf, you might not have even noticed they were there, but every one of them was chosen with real care. So naturally they became part of the manor’s scenery.”

At Ram’s words, scenes from all over the manor flashed through Garfiel’s mind.

Sure enough, he realized now—everywhere you looked, there were those subtle touches, assertive without overpowering, keeping the space from feeling empty, placed with that kind of thoughtfulness.

Even that blue vase and the flowers in it—surely the combo and placement had been considered just for that spot.

And on top of that—

“…I got so caught up in excuses, I didn’t even apologize.”

“Oh? You figured it out on your own. Then I won’t dock points for that.”

At the faint smile from the girl he adored, Garfiel ruffled his own hair in a frenzy. Then he bolted to the supply closet at the end of the hall, yanked out the contents in a rush, darted past Ram, and hurried back the way they’d come.

“Sorry ‘bout that, Ram! I’ll help Sis out myself!”

“You should’ve done that from the start. Don’t make Ram do the work.”

“Yeah! Thanks for the wake-up call! Still love ya, Ram!”

“Yes, yes.”

Garfiel scampered back down the hall to where Frederica knelt, and before she could hand over the cleaning tools, he bowed his head low. From a distance, Ram watched as Frederica—startled at first—then stroked her little brother’s lowered head, her lips curving into a gentle smile.

And—

“—What an idiot.”

The shattered vase might never forgive him, but all in all, it had served a pretty decent purpose in the end.

～Fin～
